nodes.text: Are\[2^n\pm 1\]and\[n!\pm 1\]powerful (i.e. if $p\mid m$ then $p^2\mid m$) for only finitely many $n$?

#936 : [Er76d,p.32] number theory | powerful Cushing and Pascoe [CuPa16] have shown the answer to the second question is yes assuming the abc conjecture - in fact, for any fixed $k\geq 0$, there are only finitely many $n$ and powerful $x$ such that $\lvert x-n!\rvert \leq k$. CrowdMath [Cr20] has shown that the answer to the first question is yes, again assuming the abc conjecture.
